why: Celebrating a finished mark and claiming victory over a rival overlap heavily when the celebration names the rival that fell.

why.T3-010: Neighbouring works settling lines and space with no fight to end: asking expansion to spare art, telling the room to stop beyond the approved border, and refusing r/GreenLattice's space claim outright (C1113827).
why.T3-094: Distinct from the border itself, members contest whether r/GreenLattice may approve at all: challenging the enforcer's authority (C1026486) and expanding until real art stops them rather than a ruling.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-010 carries the lines and space agreed or refused, but not the contest over whether r/GreenLattice has standing to rule on the room's build at all.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: Members dispute whether the room needs r/GreenLattice's approval and who may give it, distinct at C1026486 and C1113827.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-094; dropping it leaves the border negotiation whole but loses the dispute over the enforcer's authority.

why.T3-016: Questions and answers about the event itself: what the canvas is for, one member asking the purpose and another explaining r/place as a fun April Fools joke rather than any room claim.

why.T3-095: A claim the room did not stage, an r/Israel plan for the spot, being weighed: the respondent finds the warning was not a joke, settling whether it is real rather than judging an official joke.

why.T3-154: Victory over named rival rooms claimed: the Canucks mark remained while the Flames and Oilers logos were destroyed, the Flames wrecking celebrated, and Benning praised for the outcome.

why.T3-117: The end of the canvas itself registered: fatigue with the whole event and the judgement that it ended when it needed to, with no work mourned or celebrated.

why.T3-005: An alarm raised on the room's work: the mark reported as under attack while the build is active, the opening of a defence rather than an account of what happened.

why.T3-105: The work kept as it stood: a video shared in the aftermath and a timelapse watched to review the attempts at the Canucks mark, records of the work rather than a celebration or a story of its fights.

why.T3-095: Same material as position 3: a claim the room did not stage, an r/Israel plan for the spot, being settled as real rather than a joke.

why.T3-141: The work handed across time zones for the hours others sleep: an Australian taking the night shift, and members later recalling that the night was said to be covered.

why.T3-009: The room's own finished work marked as achieved and lasting to the end: 'we finished it', the logo survived, any victory taken this season, the mark still sharp; the Flames aside is incidental to a celebration of the room's own mark.

why.T3-087: Finding out who is behind the damage: members wondering what caused the Alberta losses and naming theblackvoid as the responsible group, tracing rather than fighting.

why.T3-073: What happened to the work told after the fact: the room entered late, began by attacking the Flames' thread instead of building, and then made its own design; an account, not a call to attack or a build report.

why.T3-142: Jokes and slurs aimed at a people over the location dispute: a 'final solution' joke, a Homeland joke about Jews, and the generalizing 'always the Jews' line.

why.T3-050: Mockery traded with a rival community over the canvas work: the other logo's disappearance taunted, limp-dick jibes returned, and a playoff taunt image linked.

why.T3-164: Comfort and support found through the canvas dispute: a Jewish Canucks fan torn between sides and a member answering with reassurance and affection, not being alone.
